ORDER APPROVING SCANA ENERGY’S 20th REQUEST FOR DISBURSEMENT FOR APRIL 2026 PAYMENTS TO THE REGULATED PROVIDER FROM THE UNIVERSAL SERVICE FUND FOR GROUP-1 CUSTOMERS

This matter comes before the Georgia Public Service Commission (“Commission”) as a result of SCANA Energy Marketing, LLC. (“SCANA Energy”) filing their monthly Request for Universal Service Fund (“USF”) Disbursement pursuant to paragraph 18.1(3) of the Consent Order.

On August 6, 2024, the Commission issued its Consent Order in the above-styled docket. The Consent Order detailed the terms and conditions under which SCANA Energy should serve as the 2024-2026 Regulated Provider. The Consent Order provided for recovery for SCANA Energy, as Regulated Provider, for bad debt of Group-1 customers; and the Commission authorized a methodology for payment of bad debt to SCANA Energy (Consent Order, ¶18). 

On July 15, 2025, the Commission approved Scana’s petition to extend the term of the regulated provider until August 31, 2027.

On March 5, 2026, SCANA Energy, as the Regulated Provider, reported to have billed and provided service to a total of 9,089 Group-1 customers. Pursuant to Paragraph 18.1 of the Consent Order, SCANA Energy shall receive one-twelfth (1/12) of $57 or $4.75 per each Group-1 customer for bad debt recovery (Consent Order, ¶18.1). The multiplication of SCANA Energy’s Group-1 customer count by the $4.75, totals to $43,172.75. 

SCANA Energy submitted the monthly customer count and a notarized sworn statement to aid in Staff’s verification of the number of Group-1 customers that were served by SCANA Energy. The company reported the total count of Group-1 and Group-2 customers. The Regulated Provider is not entitled to bad debt recovery for Group-2 customers.

*******

WHEREFORE IT IS ORDERED that the Commission hereby approves a payment of $43,172.75 from the USF to SCANA Energy based on a verified total of 9,089 Group-1 customer count, in accordance with ¶18.1 of the Consent Order.

ORDERED FURTHER, that the Commission retains the right to audit the customer counts for both Group-1 and Group-2 utilizing the records of the Regulated Provider, Atlanta Gas Light Company, the Department of Human Services and any other relevant information or documentation.

ORDERED FURTHER, nothing in this order shall be construed to be inconsistent with the terms of the Consent Order.

ORDERED FURTHER, that jurisdiction over this proceeding is expressly retained for the purpose of entering such further order or orders as this Commission deems proper.

ORDERED FURTHER, any motion for reconsideration, rehearing, or oral argument shall not stay the effectiveness of this order unless expressly ordered by the Commission.

The above by action of the Commission in Administrative Session on the 16th day of June, 2026.

______________ ________________
Sallie Tanner Jason Shaw 
Executive Secretary Chairman

_______________ _________________

IN RE: ATLANTA GAS LIGHT COMPANY’S UNIVERSAL SERVICE FUND FACILITIES EXPANSION PLAN

FINAL ORDER APPROVING ATLANTA GAS LIGHT COMPANY’S PETITION TO AMEND THE 2026 UNIVERSAL SERVICE FUND FACILITIES EXPANSION PLAN
WHEELER COUNTY PROJECT

Background

Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 46-2-20, 46-2-21, and 46-2-23, the Commission has general jurisdiction over natural gas companies. The Commission also administers the Georgia Natural Gas Competition and Deregulation Act, O.C.G.A. § 46-4-150 et seq. The Commission administers the USF pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 46-4-161. As provided in O.C.G.A. § 46-4-161(a)(2) and (g)(1), the Commission shall consider proposed USF funded line-extension projects with a number of factors, including whether the proposed new facility is in the public interest. The distributions during any fiscal year shall not exceed $25 million, O.C.G.A. § 46-4-161(b), and it shall not exceed five percent of the EDC’s capital budget, O.C.G.A. § 46-4-161(g)(2).

Atlanta Gas Light Company’s Petition 

On June 2, 2026, Atlanta Gas Light Company (“AGL” or “Company”) filed its Petition for Approval of Jeff Davis Project and Wheeler Project as Amendment to 2025 and 2026 Universal Service Fund Facilities Expansion Plans to Replace the Emanuel County Project..

Commission Rule 515-7-5-.07(1) and (2) outlines the process and requirements for AGL to file a USF a Facilities Expansion Plan. In accordance with Commission Rule 515-7-5-.07(2)(a)-(g), AGL filed seven (7) Minimum Filing Requirements (MFRs). The MFRs included the following:
MFR-1: Written description of each project
MFR-2: AGL capital budget
MFR-3: Stakeholder process
MFR-4: Maps of each project
MFR-5: Basic economic development data
MFR-6: Project Financial Analysis
MFR-7: Project Technical Analysis

The Staff reviewed AGL’s filing, and found it to be whole and complete. 

Commission Decision

During the July 7, 2026 Administrative Session, the Commission approved the Wheeler County Project with the following Motion from Commissioner Tricia Pridemore:

I have a motion concerning the Wheeler County Project filed as part of AGL’s June 2nd petition. 
I move that the Emanuel County Project approved for $33,175,940 ($33.1 million Rounded) as part of the 2025 USF Facilities Expansion Plan will be replaced with and have its funds shifted to the Wheeler County Project that was filed as part of AGL’s amendment to the 2025 and the 2026 USF Facilities Expansion Plan. This will include $22,345,586 ($22.3 million Rounded) from the 2025 USF budget and $5,413,585 ($5.413 million Rounded) from the 2026 USF budget. The remaining $5,4,16,769 ($5.416 million Rounded) will be released for future projects. 

* * * * *

Ordering Paragraphs

WHEREFORE IT IS ORDERED, that the Commission approves Atlanta Gas Light Company’s Petition for approval of the Wheeler County Project as an amendment to the 2025 and 2026 Universal Service Fund Facilities Expansion Plans to Replace the Emanuel County Project, finding the Wheeler County Project to be in the public interest. 
ORDERED FURTHER, that the Commission approves that the Emanuel County Project, approved for $33,175,940 as part of the 2025 USF Facilities Expansion Plan, to be replaced with and have its funds shifted to the Wheeler County Project that was filed as part of AGL’s Amendment to the 2025 and the 2026 USF Facilities Expansion Plan.

ORDERED FURTHER, that the Commission approves that from the USF funds from the Emanuel County Project, $22,345,586 from the 2025 USF budget, and $5,413,585 from the 2026 USF budget, is shifted to the Wheeler County Project. The remaining $5,416,769 related to the Emanuel County Project under the 2026 USF will be released for future projects. 

ORDERED FURTHER, that all findings, conclusions, statements, and directives made by the Commission and contained in the foregoing sections of this Order are hereby adopted as findings of fact, conclusions of law, statements of regulatory policy, and orders of this Commission.

ORDERED FURTHER, that a motion for reconsideration, rehearing, or oral argument or any other motion shall not stay the effective date of this Order, unless otherwise ordered by the Commission.

ORDERED FURTHER, that jurisdiction over this matter is expressly retained for the purpose of entering such further Order or Orders as the Commission may deem just and proper. 

The above by action of the Commission in Administrative Session on the 7th day of July 2026.

Sallie Tanner Jason Shaw
Executive Secretary Chairman

Date Date

The Commission approved the Jeff Davis Project portion of the Petition on June 29, 2026.

ORDER AMENDING THE COUNTYWIDE SAFETY PLAN, CERTIFICATES, AND WAIVER OF HEARING REQUIRMENTS
These matters come before the Georgia Public Service Commission (“Commission”) as a result of Atlanta Gas Light Company (“AGL”), Liberty Utilities (Peach State Natural Gas) Corp. (“Liberty”), and the City of Grantville (“Grantville”) filing an Amended Joint Petition to amend a Countywide Safety Plan (“CWSP”), amend the Certificates, and waive the associated hearing requirements.

I. JURISDICTION
The Commission has the power and authority to enforce the provisions of: Ga. Const. Art. 9, § 6, ¶ 2, O.C.G.A. §§ 46-2-20, 46-2-21, 46-2-30, 46-2-50, 46-2-51, 46-2-52, 46-2-53, 46-2-54, 46-2-57, 46-2-58, 46-2-59, 46-2-71, 46-2-90, 46-2-91, 46-2-92, 46-2-93, 46-4-21, 46-4-22, 46-4-23, 46-4-24, 46-4-25, 46-4-26, 46-4-27, 46-4-28, 46-4-29, 46-4-30, 46-4-31, and 50-13-1 et seq., applicable to Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity and Safety of Natural Gas Pipelines/Distribution systems regulated by the Commission. The applicable Commission Rules involved are, inter alia, at 515-7-1-.01 et. seq., 515-9-1-.01 et. seq., 515-9-3-3.01 et seq., 515-9-6-.01 et. Seq., and 515-9-7-.01.

The Commission further has jurisdiction over Georgia intrastate natural gas operators pursuant to inter alia: 49 U.S.C. §§ 60105 and 60122; Rules and Regulations prescribed by the United States Department of Transportation applicable to the "Transportation of Natural and Other Gas by Pipeline: Minimum Safety Standards" (49 C.F.R. Parts 40, 191, 192, 193 and 199) having been made the Rules and Regulations of the Commission for the safe installation and operation of all natural gas transmission and distribution facilities by companies subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission.

II. PROCEDURAL HISTORY

On March 16, 2026, AGL, Liberty, and Grantville filed an amended Joint Petition to amend the Meriwether Countywide Safety Plan (Docket No. 29309, Document No. 225870). The purpose of the amendment is to divide the unserved and unassigned area so that new customers will be able to receive natural gas service in a timelier manner. Currently, AGL and Liberty are the only signatories to the Meriwether CWSP. The proposed amended CWSP also adds Grantville to the CWSP. Grantville will have assigned territory in the northwest corner of Meriwether County.
On March 23, 2026, AGL filed an updated application to amend its Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity for Meriwether County (Docket No. 30300, Document No. 225984). AGL is seeking to amend its Certificate to conform its Certificate boundaries with the safety-based boundaries requested in the Meriwether CWSP. AGL will be providing the same distribution service that it currently provides and using the same source of gas that it currently uses.
On January 30, 2026, Liberty filed an application to amend its Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity for Meriwether County (Docket No. 41159, Document No. 225287). Liberty is seeking to amend its current Certificate to conform its current Certificate boundaries with the safety-based boundaries. Liberty will be providing the same distribution service that it currently provides and was previously certificated to provide.
Initially, Atlanta Gas Light Company and Liberty jointly petitioned for Expedited Approval to Amend the Countywide Safety Plan for Meriwether County and Waive the Hearing Requirement on August 21, 2024 (Docket No. 29309, Document No. 219731). The petition sought to divide the unserved and unassigned area within Meriwether County. AGL and Liberty were the only signatories to the Meriwether CWSP. The proposed revisions were for Boundary 1 and a new Boundary 2 between AGL and Liberty to expand both operators’ territories to include the previously unassigned territory.
On August 21, 2024, AGL filed an Application for an Amended Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity for Meriwether County (Docket No. 30300, Document No. 219730) to conform its Certificate boundaries with the safety-based boundaries requested in the Joint Petition to Amend the Meriwether CWSP.
On August 22, 2024, Liberty filed an Application for an Amended Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity for Meriwether County (Docket No. 41159, Document No. 219732) to conform its Certificate boundaries with the safety-based boundaries requested in the Joint Petition to Amend the Meriwether CWSP.
On September 5, 2024, the Cities of Hogansville and Grantville, Georgia filed an Objection to the Joint Petition stating that they have interests in Meriwether County regarding territory and boundaries. Hogansville supplies natural gas to Liberty’s system, which serves the Meriwether County Industrial Park. Hogansville desired to ensure its allowance to continue providing natural gas to the Industrial Park without issue. Grantville annexed parts of Meriwether County in 2021 and can extend its natural gas system there without certification by the Commission. Subsequent filings were made by the AGL and Liberty regarding the objection. AGL, Liberty, Hogansville, and Grantville conducted negotiations and arrived at an agreement with respect to the territories and boundaries, which are reflected in the March 16, 2026, filing (Docket No. 29309, Document No. 225870).
The Meriwether CWSP was last amended on June 5, 2018. AGL’s Certificate was last amended on April 19, 2012. Liberty’s Certificate has not been amended since it was approved by this Commission on June 5, 2018. Grantville has home county status. 
The Commission’s Facilities Protection Unit has reviewed the proposed requests and has no objection.

III. STAFF REVIEW AND RECOMMENDATION
The Staff has reviewed and performed its due diligence of the Petitions. The Facilities Protection Unit inspected the proposed boundaries and waivers and has no objections to the requests. 

Staff recommends that the Commission grant the amendment to the CWSP, Certificate Amendments, and waivers of the associated hearing requirements. 

IV. FINDINGS OF FACT AND CONCLUSIONS OF LAW

THE COMMISSION FINDS AND CONCLUDES that it has jurisdiction over natural gas utilities. (O.C.G.A. § 46-2-20). Specifically, the Commission maintains safety jurisdiction over all natural gas transmission and distribution facilities within Georgia, including those natural gas facilities that are owned and operated by municipalities. (O.C.G.A. § 46-2-20(i)). The Commission further has jurisdiction over Georgia intrastate natural gas operators pursuant to inter alia: 49 U.S.C.S. §§ 60105 and 60122, 49 C.F.R. Part 191, 49 C.F.R. Part 192; O.C.G.A. §§ 46-2-21, 46-2-30, 46-2-53, 46-2-90, 46-2-91, 46-4-1, 46-4-20 et. seq., 50-13-1 et seq.; and Commission Rules 515-7-1-.01 et. seq., 515-9-1-.01 et. seq., 515-9-3-.01 et. seq., 515-9-6-.01 and 515-9-7-.01 et. seq.

THE COMMISSION FURTHER FINDS AND CONCLUDES that Atlanta Gas Light Company, Liberty Utilities (Peach State Natural Gas) Corp., and the City of Grantville are each individually and collectively subject to the safety jurisdiction of the Commission.

THE COMMISSION FURTHER FINDS AND CONCLUDES that the Commission’s Facilities Protection Unit Staff has the authority to inspect the facilities of all Georgia natural gas providers pursuant to the legal citations contained supra.

THE COMMISSION FURTHER FINDS AND CONCLUDES that the Atlanta Gas Light Company, Liberty Utilities (Peach State Natural Gas) Corp., and the City of Grantville hereby waive any hearings and/or further findings or conclusions of law with respect to the above-styled matters and agree that the Commission may enter an order based upon the agreement of Atlanta Gas Light Company, Liberty Utilities (Peach State Natural Gas) Corp., and the City of Grantville, to comport their respective territories to the safety-based boundaries agreed to in the Joint Consent Agreement attached hereto and the Countywide Safety Plans agreed to by the Operators and Staff (attached as Exhibit “A” to the Consent Agreement and “C” (Maps) thereto). The Meriwether Countywide Safety Plan Consent Agreement, Plan and Plan Map(s) are all incorporated into this order as if specifically written herein.

THE COMMISSION FURTHER FINDS AND CONCLUDES that the CWSP for Meriwether County (see Exhibit "A" to the Consent Agreement (Attachment “One”)) agreed to by the Operators and Staff, shall be the CWSP for Meriwether County until otherwise ordered by the Commission.

THE COMMISSION FURTHER FINDS AND CONCLUDES that compliance with all parts of the CWSP for Meriwether County (id.) shall begin immediately upon issuance of this Commission Order. All timelines and action items contained within the Consent Agreement and Meriwether CWSP shall be incorporated by reference into the body of this Order Adopting Consent Agreement as if specifically written herein and the failure of the Operators to meet all such timelines and/ or act on all such action items shall be a violation of this Order.

THE COMMISSION FURTHER FINDS AND CONCLUDES that all changes to the CWSP for Meriwether County shall be made in accordance with inter alia, Commission Rule 515-9-7-.01 et. seq.

THE COMMISSION FURTHER FINDS AND CONCLUDES that Atlanta Gas Light Company’s Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity shall be granted to conform to the safety-based boundaries agreed to by Staff and the Meriwether County Operators in accordance with the CWSP/Maps attached hereto. (Exhibit “A” to the Joint Consent Agreement and Attachments “A” and “C” thereto respectively (for the Plan and Plan Maps)). 

THE COMMISSION FURTHER FINDS AND CONCLUDES that Liberty Utilities (Peach State Natural Gas) Corp.’s Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity shall be granted to conform to the safety-based boundaries agreed to by Staff and the Meriwether County Operators in accordance with the CWSP/Maps attached hereto. (Exhibit “A” to the Joint Consent Agreement and Attachments “A” and “C” thereto respectively (for the Plan and Plan Maps)).

THE COMMISSION FURTHER FINDS AND CONCLUDES that based on the Commission’s review of the proposed CWSP/Maps and Certificate Application submitted, that such agreements by the Operators are respectively, a reasonable and appropriate resolution of the CWSP and Certificate proceedings for Meriwether County, Georgia.

THE COMMISSION FURTHER FINDS that Atlanta Gas Light Company, Liberty Utilities (Peach State Natural Gas) Corp., and the City of Grantville request for informal disposition and waiver of hearing pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 50-13-13(4) is granted, and that the informal disposition is appropriate given the agreement of all affected Meriwether County operators to the proffered CWSP.

THE COMMISSION FURTHER FINDS AND CONCLUDES that the executed Joint Consent Agreement and the Meriwether CWSP/Maps attached hereto, are hereby adopted by the Commission, and shall constitute a final resolution of the Meriwether CWSP and related Certificate docket.

VI. ORDERING PARAGRAPHS

WHEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that all findings of fact and conclusions of law contained within the preceding sections of this Order are hereby adopted as the findings and conclusions of this Commission.

ORDERED FURTHER, that a motion for reconsideration, rehearing or oral argument or any other motion shall not stay the effective date of this Order unless otherwise ordered by the Commission.

ORDERED FURTHER, that jurisdiction over this matter is expressly retained for the purpose of entering such further Order or Orders as this Commission may deem just and proper.

The above by action of the Commission in Administrative Session on the 7th day of July 2026.

__________________________ ___________________________
Sallie Tanner Jason Shaw
Executive Secretary Chairman

__________________________ ___________________________

DOCKET NO. 57171

PROCEDURAL AND SCHEDULING ORDER

In Re: Docket No. 57171: Real Time Pricing (“RTP”) Revenue Credit and Allocation Methodology

I. BACKGROUND 

The May 28, 2026, Short Order Adopting Stipulation in Docket 56765 required that the “Commission shall further review the methodology by which the Company credits Real-Time Pricing (“RTP”) revenue to the FCR revenues and the allocations the Company is making under such methodology in this Docket. This proceeding shall be concluded by December 31, 2026, and the Commission may make modifications if appropriate. The implementation of such modifications, if any, shall be credited to fuel revenues as determined by the Commission, and any corresponding change to base revenues shall be recorded in a regulatory asset or liability and addressed in the next base rate case. As part of such proceeding, the Company shall provide Commission Staff, within 45 days of the date of the order adopting this Stipulation, complete hourly RTP generation and dispatch data including cost and energy (MWhs) for the FCR-27 historical period and projections for the current FCR-27 period. Staff may issue data requests seeking additional information related to the methodology and allocations.”

II. PRELIMINARY DIRECTIVES 

The Commission orders this Procedural and Scheduling Order to establish discovery procedures and establish a hearing schedule. The Public Interest Advocacy (“PIA”) Staff is appointed as the agent for the Commission for discovery purposes. Georgia Power Company is hereby made a party and shall be bound by the Commission’s rulings in this docket and is directed to publish notice of this proceeding. 

Pursuant to the Commission’s Utility Rule 515-2-1-.04(3), Georgia Power is directed to give first notice of the proceedings in this docket no later than 30 days after filing its application.

These proceedings shall be considered as a contested case under O.C.G.A. § 50-13-13. These proceedings also encompass complex litigation as that term is used in O.C.G.A. § 9-11-33(a) and discovery procedures apply accordingly.

Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 50-13-13, this proceeding shall be considered a contested case. As such, the Commission hereby designates the following staff members to act as PIA Staff in this proceeding:

Tom Newsome
Rob Trokey 
Jason Forsythe
Shemetha Jones
Justin Pawluk
Chris Collado

Jamie Barber

The PIA Staff shall be responsible for performing an independent evaluation of the filed case from the standpoint of promoting the public interest and just and reasonable rates and advocating for that position. The PIA Staff is considered a party to the case and may negotiate settlements with other parties, in the public interest.

The Commission hereby designates the following Staff members to act as Commissioner Advisory Staff in this proceeding: 

Steve Roetger
Antonio Alera
Ruth Somuah
Alicia McBride
William Threatt
Keimani Harvey

The Commissioner Advisory Staff shall not be a party to this case, but shall act as a technical advisor to the Commissioners, and shall advise Commissioners upon request based exclusively on its own independent evaluation of the facts contained in the record.

The Commission authorizes the PIA Staff to issue discovery pursuant to O.C.G.A. 46-2-57(a). The PIA Staff may conduct depositions and use any other methods of formal and informal discovery in this docket. The use of any informal discovery methods shall not augment or abridge existing discovery rights and responsibilities. 

O.C.G.A. 46-2-26(d) provides that "[t]he staff and formal intervenors shall have the right to examine all utility records used in the preparation of the testimony and exhibits of the utility."  
III. HEARING SCHEDULE, FILING DATES AND PROCEDURES

In compliance with the Short Order Adopting the Stipulation in Docket 56765, the Company shall provide Commission Staff complete hourly RTP generation and dispatch data including cost and energy (MWhs) for the FCR-27 historical period and projections for the current FCR-27 period.

INTERVENTION AND HEARING PROCEDURES

The following are procedures to which the parties should adhere with respect to this docket.
1. Intervention
Intervention Period

Any person or party, on whom a statute does not confer an unconditional right to intervene, must file an application for leave to intervene within 30 days following the first published notice of the proceeding. Pursuant to Rule 515-2-1-.04(3), Georgia Power will be directed to give first notice of its proceedings in this case not later than August 7, 2026.

Application Requirements

(b) In addition to the requirements prescribed by O.C.G.A. § 46-2-59 for applications for leave to intervene, the application must (1) identify other intervening parties or intervening party applications whose interest is similar to that of the applicant, along with an explanation of why the identified intervening party or intervening party applicant will not adequately represent the applicant’s interest; and (2) state the applicant’s present intention to submit direct testimony and by whom and on what subject. The requirements identified herein shall constitute a continuing obligation of the applicant or intervening party. 

Late Applications for Intervention

(c) Any application for leave to intervene filed late must state the reason why such application was not submitted within 30 days of first published notice. Objections to late intervention applications must be filed in conformance with the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 46-2-59-(d).

Rulings on Intervention Applications

(d) The Commission will take up and rule on applications for leave to intervene at the first hearing date set in this docket.

2. Service

Each party has the responsibility to serve copies of any documents filed with the Commission upon each intervenor and intervenor applicant. Furthermore, in the case of documents filed prior to the deadline for intervention established above, copies shall also be served upon each party indicated in the Certificate of Service accompanying this Order.

3. Witnesses’ Testimony 
(a) Summations of direct testimony will take no longer than fifteen (15) minutes or, at the discretion of the Commission, no longer than thirty (30) minutes.

(b) Summations should be limited to testimony and exhibits in the pre-filed testimony.

(c) Demonstrative handouts intended to be used during summations of the pre-filed testimony or in opening or closing statements, if applicable, must be pre-filed at least five (5) days prior to the hearing and must be limited to the scope of the testimony and exhibits in the pre-filed testimony.

 (d) Except for good cause shown, corrections to testimony must be pre-filed at least five (5) days prior to the hearing.

 (e) In the absence of a valid objection made and sustained to pre-filed testimony, the pre-filed testimony and exhibits, with corrections, will be admitted into the record as if orally given prior to the witness’ summation, subject to a motion to strike after admission or other relevant objection.

Where the testimony of a panel of witnesses is presented, cross-examination may either be addressed to the panel, in which case any member of the panel may answer, or cross-examination may be addressed to an individual panel member, in which case that panel member shall give the answer; provided, however, that any other panel member shall be allowed to supplement the answer given.

Motions to strike any portion of pre-filed testimony must be filed at least two days prior to the hearing. 

Any individual that presents testimony during this proceeding may not conduct cross examination of other parties.

4. Hearing Exhibits

For the record in all hearings, it shall be the responsibility of the parties sponsoring any hearing exhibits to ensure that the Hearing Reporter and all parties of record receive copies of the hearing exhibits at the time of introducing the exhibits at the hearings. (Exhibits filed with pre-filed testimony should already have been provided, as per Commission Rule 515-2-1-.04(3).)
Procedures and Forms for Making an Application to Intervene

Applications to intervene and Commission approval thereof are covered by Official Code of Georgia Annotated § 46-2-59, and the Commission’s Utility Rule 515-2-1-.06. Each applicant shall submit their application to intervene to the Commission, addressed to the Executive Secretary, Ms. Sallie Tanner, 244 Washington St. S.W., Atlanta, Georgia 30334-5701.

In addition, each applicant shall submit a copy of their application to Georgia Power, and all other parties who have applied to intervene, and submit a Certificate of Service to the Commission certifying that these copies have been served on the other parties. To obtain a list of other applicants to intervene, contact Ms. Quawanda Boyer, Georgia Public Service Commission, 244 Washington St., S.W., Atlanta, Georgia 30334-5701, (Telephone: 404-463-2893).
Specialized Testimony and Assistance
Specialized testimony and assistance are required to review Georgia Power Company’s RTP program in this proceeding. Accordingly, the Commission hereby sets forth the scope and budget for such testimony and assistance. The scope is testimony and assistance necessary for the PIA Staff to make an informed presentation and recommendation to the Commission regarding evaluation of Georgia Power Company’s RTP program. The budget for such testimony and assistance is $80,250. 

O.C.G.A. § 46-2-33(b) provides that all invoices relating to the testimony and assistance shall be subject to Commission review and approval, and no utility shall be required to pay any invoice not approved by the Commission. Accordingly, the consultants providing the testimony and assistance shall submit their invoices to the Commission. Such invoices shall be reviewed and approved using the Commission’s existing process for approval of consultant invoices, as such process may be modified by the Commission from time to time. Upon receiving approved invoices, Georgia Power Company shall promptly remit payment to the consulting firm. 

O.C.G.A. § 46-2-33(c) provides that the amounts paid by regulated companies under this Code section shall be deemed a necessary cost of providing service, and the utility shall be entitled to recover the full amount of any costs charged to the utility pursuant to this Code section. O.C.G.A. § 46-2-33(c) further provides that, at the election of the utility, the utility shall be entitled to recover all such costs promptly through a reasonably designed rider designated for such purpose. 

The Commission hereby determines that specialized testimony and assistance is required in Docket No. 57171. Accordingly, the Commission hereby sets forth the scope and budget for such assistance as described below.

FINAL ORDER APPROVING ATLANTA GAS LIGHT COMPANY’S PETITION TO AMEND THE 2026 UNIVERSAL SERVICE FUND FACILITIES EXPANSION PLAN
JEFF DAVIS COUNTY PROJECT

Background

Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 46-2-20, 46-2-21, and 46-2-23, the Commission has general jurisdiction over natural gas companies. The Commission also administers the Georgia Natural Gas Competition and Deregulation Act, O.C.G.A. § 46-4-150 et seq. The Commission administers the USF pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 46-4-161. As provided in O.C.G.A. § 46-4-161(a)(2) and (g)(1), the Commission shall consider proposed USF funded line-extension projects with a number of factors, including whether the proposed new facility is in the public interest. The distributions during any fiscal year shall not exceed $25 million, O.C.G.A. § 46-4-161(b), and it shall not exceed five percent of the EDC’s capital budget, O.C.G.A. § 46-4-161(g)(2).

Atlanta Gas Light Company’s Petition 

On June 2, 2026, AGL filed an Amended 2026 Universal Service Fund (“USF”) Facilities Expansion Plan (“Amended 2026 USF Plan-III”), which included the Jeff Davis County Project.

Commission Rule 515-7-5-.07(1) and (2) outlines the process and requirements for an Electric Distribution Company (“EDC”) to file a USF Annual Plan. In accordance with Commission Rule 515-7-5-.07(2)(a)-(g), AGL filed seven (7) Minimum Filing Requirements (MFRs). The MFRs included the following:

MFR-1: Written description of each project
MFR-2: AGL capital budget
MFR-3: Stakeholder process
MFR-4: Maps of each project
MFR-5: Basic economic development data
MFR-6: Project Financial Analysis
MFR-7: Project Technical Analysis

MFR-1 Project Description: Jeff Davis County Project

AGL proposed to serve the new Jeff Davis County Primary School in Hazlehurst, Georgia. The Jeff Davis County Board of Education is investing $32 million in the school’s construction. AGL stated that the school plans to utilize natural gas for space heating, water heating, cooking, and a backup generator. 

To serve the site, AGL proposed to tie-into existing 2-inch plastic on Pat Dixon Road east of its intersection with of Pat Dixon Road and Buford Road and install approximately 1,945 feet of 2-inch plastic (MAOP 60 psi) along Pat Dixon Road to reach the school. The school also requires an approximate 600-foot 2-inch plastic service line.

AGL also identified a pressure improvement necessary to remove a system constraint. The Company proposes to install approximately 1,525 feet of 2-inch plastic (MAOP 60 psi) along Collins Street and retire approximately 1,525 feet of 1-1/4-inch MHP steel pipe. The existing 1-1/4-inch MHP steel pipe proposed for retirement is connected to 2-inch pipe on both ends presenting a bottleneck that must be removed.

MFR-2 Capital Budgets 

AGL did not file an MFR-2 because it was provided as part of the original USF 2026 Plan filing on November 25, 2025. There have been no changes to its 2026 capital budgets. 

MFR-3 Stakeholder Process 

AGL did not file an MFR-3 because it was provided as part of the original USF 2026 Plan filing on November 25, 2025. There are no updates to the stakeholder process.
MFR-4 Maps

AGL provided maps related to the proposed project. 
MFR-5 Basic Economic Development Data 

For the Jeff Davis County Project, AGL stated that the construction of the new school would create 130 jobs associated with the $32 million investment. 

MFR-5
+

MFR-6 Financial Technical Analysis 

AGL listed an engineering estimate of $330,000. With income taxes and finance costs, the total USF request was $383,661. 
MFR-7 Project Technical Analysis

In MFR-7, AGL provided technical specifications for each line-extension project, including gas load, PSI, pipe lengths, wall thickness, and other engineering details. 

Staff Analysis: Jeff Davis County Project

The Staff performed its due diligence by reviewing the filed MFR’s. The Staff reviewed MFR-1 related to the description of the project. For MFR-2, the Company’s 2026 capital budget was filed public disclosure as part of the 2025 – 2034 Integrated Capacity and Delivery Plan (“i-CDP”) Final Order in Docket No. 43820. The 2026 capital budget was $687,051,667, and the 5% budget cap was $34,352,583. There is a $25,000,000 budget restriction, and for 2026, there is $9,694,081 unencumbered and available. There are no issues with funding the project. Regarding MFR-3, there was not any new information provided from the original USF 2026 Plan filing. The Staff reviewed the map of the project shown in MFR, and the Staff used Google Maps to review the project sites. In MFR-5, the Staff reviewed the economic development information. The Staff reviewed MFR-6 for the Cost to Serve, and found that AGL had rounded the dollar amounts. The original MFR-6 used an engineering estimate of $330,000 before income taxes and finance costs. The Staff used the exact numbers for the engineering estimate at $333,224. With income taxes and finance costs added, the total project request was $387,409. Regarding MFR-7, AGL listed that the expected gas load was 6,779 cubic foot per hour. It included the same dollar amounts and pipe facilities and cost estimates as MFR-6. AGL has stated that it has an Asset Development Process (“ADP”) utilized to generate construction estimates. ADP consists of five stage gates that develop and refine project estimates. ADP prescribes that the first stage gate includes a +50%/-30% interval to account for unknowns that cannot be foreseen in preparing a stage gate 1 estimate. As the project progresses, the estimate is refined through stage gates 2 through 5 as unknowns are identified. Stage gate 1 estimates are typically presented to the Commission with USF projects. The Staff found the MFR’s to be whole and complete.

Commission Decision

At the June 16, 2026 Administrative Session, the Commission approved Atlanta Gas Light Company’s Petition to Amend the 2026 Universal Service Fund Facilities Expansion Plan for the Jeff Davis County Project finding it to be in the public interest with a total estimated Cost to Serve of $387,409.33.

* * * * *

Ordering Paragraphs

WHEREFORE IT IS ORDERED, that the Commission approves Atlanta Gas Light Company’s Petition to Amend the 2026 Universal Service Fund Facilities Expansion Plan for the Jeff Davis County Project finding it to be in the public interest. 
ORDERED FURTHER, that the Commission approves an estimated cost of $387,409.33 for the Jeff Davis County Project. 

ORDERED FURTHER, that all findings, conclusions, statements, and directives made by the Commission and contained in the foregoing sections of this Order are hereby adopted as findings of fact, conclusions of law, statements of regulatory policy, and orders of this Commission.

ORDERED FURTHER, that a motion for reconsideration, rehearing, or oral argument or any other motion shall not stay the effective date of this Order, unless otherwise ordered by the Commission.

ORDER APPROVING AMENDMENTS TO ATLANTA GAS LIGHT COMPANY’S 2025 – 2034 INTEGRATED CAPACITY AND DELIVERY PLAN

Background

On February 23, 2021, the Commission approved the Order Adopting a Stipulation in Docket No. 42315. The Stipulation adopted that was submitted by Staff and AGL (the “Governance Document”) that allowed the Company to file, for the Commission’s consideration, a comprehensive planning tool, referred to as the Integrated Capacity and Delivery Plan (“i-CDP” or the “Plan”). The Plan’s purpose is to help ensure consistency and continuity of the forecasts, assumptions, selected options, and other planning parameters that the Company files within the independent Capacity Supply Plan (“CSP”) and Georgia Rate Adjustment Mechanism (“GRAM”) processes. The Commission approved the Company’s first i-CDP, the 2022-2031 i-CDP, on November 18, 2021. 
On February 1, 2024, AGL filed its 2025-2034 i-CDP in this docket, along with pre-filed supporting direct testimony, a Petition for Approval of the Plan, and the other minimum filing requirements established in the Stipulation Governance Document. AGL included within its February 1, 2024 filing, a request for an amendment to year 2024 of the 2022-2031 i-CDP to allow for more operational flexibility by shifting dollars between the GRAM – Safety and Compliance and the GRAM – Other budget categories and to continue this operational flexibility of shifting dollars between GRAM budget categories in this 2025-2034 i-CDP and future i-CDPs. On February 8, 2024, the Commission issued its Procedural and Scheduling Order in this Docket, which set forth the dates for filing of testimony and briefs, as well as the dates for the hearings in this matter. This proceeding was deemed complex litigation pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 9-11-33(a). 

On May 9, 2024, AGL filed an amendment to the 2025-2034 i-CDP to amend the narrative document of the 2025-2034 i-CDP to correct tables under “Figure 5.10: Bill Impacts” and to update the filing date and file name as “amended.”

On May 14, 2024, Staff filed direct testimony in response to the Company’s direct case in this docket, along with the Direct Testimony, Exhibits, and the 2024 Affiliate Audit Report by Kennedy and Associates. On May 29, 2024, the Commission issued an order revising the filing date for rebuttal testimony. On June 3, 2024, the Commission again issued an order extending the filing date for rebuttal testimony. AGL and Staff negotiated a workable compromise that would meet the Commission Staff’s and the Company’s goals while protecting the public interest. On June 10, 2024, AGL, Staff, and the Intervening Marketers filed a Stipulation. AGL also filed amended Minimum Filing Requirements on June 11, 2024. The Commission held a hearing in this docket on the stipulation on June 12, 2024. AGL, Staff, and the Named Marketers stipulated to enter into the record the pre-filed direct testimony in support of the Company’s direct case and the pre-filed direct testimony of Staff and waived cross examination of the pre-filed direct testimony. 

This matter came before the Commission at the regularly scheduled Energy Committee on June 27, 2024. On July 2, 2024, at its regularly scheduled Administrative Session, the Commission voted to approve AGL’s 2025-2034 i-CDP as amended on May 9, 2024, and as modified by the Stipulation.

Governance Document Section-5 

As provided in the Governance Document in Section-5, if there are certain factors and circumstances that may require AGL to deviate from an approved i-CDP, an amendment to the Plan for consideration must be filed. Such factors and circumstances could include, but not be limited to, changes to FERC-regulated interstate suppliers’ planned additions that affect a planned AGL intrastate project, new compliance regulations, newly discovered risks, revised assessments of previously known risks, shifts in customer growth and retention patterns, accelerated local, state and federal infrastructure projects, and other factors that require that AGL reprioritize projects within an existing i-CDP. 

Atlanta Gas Light Company’s Petition to Amend the 2025 – 2034 i-CDP

On May 14, 2026, AGL filed a petition to amend the 2025 – 2034 i-CDP. The Company requested two amendments to the Plan as a result of additional interstate pipeline capacity becoming available to AGL’s system and capital budget over- and underspending. 
Prior to the Company’s filing, Staff had meetings with AGL to discuss its amendment requests. Section-5 of the Governance Document allows for an i-CDP to be amended but does not provide for the process. Staff and AGL collaborated to agree to a process for an amendment filing. As part of this process, Staff researched and analyzed a number of items for inclusion in the filing. Staff reviewed the capital budgets and projects approved by the Commission in the 2025-2034 i-CDP. Staff also reviewed the GRAM, SRR and Cherokee LNG quarterly reports to determine actual budget progress. Staff reviewed AGL’s preliminary documents, which included a draft petition and a PowerPoint presentation. Staff reviewed the SNG and Transco websites to gather information on the interstate pipeline projects, Southern Natural Gas South System Expansion 4 Project (“SSE”) and the Transco South East Supply Enhancement Project (“SEP”). These were mentioned in the i-CDP as potential capacity projects on the interstate pipeline (Chapter 4, page 32 of AGL’s 2025-2034 i-CDP). Transco held an open season for shippers interested in the SEP project in July 2023. At the time of the 2025-3034 i-CDP filing, there was no affirmative information that each project was guaranteed to move forward at the time of the filing in 2024. 
Prior to the filing of the 2025 – 2028 Capacity Supply Plan, information was provided that the two projects were approved for construction, and AGL’s participation in the projects was approved in the 2025 – 2028 CSP. AGL subscribed to 200,000 Dth/d of firm transportation capacity in the SSE project and 75,000 Dth/d of firm transportation capacity in the SEP project. AGL acquired interstate capacity for SEP, which is expected to be in-service in late 2027, in time for the 2027-2028 heating season. AGL also acquired capacity for SSE, which is expected to be in service in late 2028. 
On April 6, 2026, AGL provided a draft Amendment for Staff’s review. Staff added more details about each of the amendment items to the draft Amendment. AGL also provided amended MFRs for Staff’s review. As part of the collaborative process, Staff and AGL agreed to the language in the amendment filing.
The first amendment is the result of the SSE and SEP projects, which will allow additional interstate pipeline capacity to become available to AGL’s system. This amendment would add four (4) tap stations and one (1) Riverdale LNG tap meter to the System Reinforcement Rider (“SRR”) for recovery. The filing included amendments to MFR-1 and MFR-3 to supplement the Company’s requested amendment to the SRR.
The second amendment is related to the Cherokee LNG expansion, where construction activity has exceeded the approved 2025 – 2027 capital budgets. The 2025 – 2027 GRAM and the SRR actual capital budget activity are underspending. This amendment would allow the 2025 – 2027 total GRAM capital budget amount, the total 2025 – 2027 SRR capital budget amount, and the 2025 – 2027 Cherokee LNG Tracker total capital budget amount to be combined to allow Cherokee LNG Tracker overspending to be absorbed by the underspending in the GRAM and SRR capital budgets. The aggregate three-year capital budget of the projects in the amended Plan would not exceed the total Commission-approved three-year capital budget of the projects, $1.869 billion. (Figure 1).

First Amendment to Add Four (4) Tap Stations and One (1) Riverdale LNG Tap Meter to the 2025-2034 i-CDP SRR Projects

As part of the first amendment request, AGL seeks an amendment to upgrade four (4) tap stations and one (1) Riverdale LNG tap meter to the SRR for recovery. These projects are related to Southern Natural Gas Company, L.L.C. (“SNG”) and the Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Corporation (“Transco”) upgrading their systems to bring additional natural gas capacity to Georgia. 
The Southern Natural Gas South System Expansion 4 Project (“SSE”) is a project that will run parallel to SNG’s South Main Line, along existing pipelines in Mississippi, Alabama, and Georgia. This project will provide 200,000 Dth/day of new capacity to AGL’s system. Transco South East Supply Enhancement Project (“SEP”) is an expansion of the existing Transco pipeline’s capacity in the southeastern United States and will provide reliable natural gas deliveries to Virginia, the Carolinas, Georgia and Alabama. This project will provide 75,000 Dth/day of new capacity to AGL’s system.

To receive and deliver the additional capacity on its system, AGL must increase the capacity of its facilities. The following stations are being upgraded as a result of the interstate pipeline projects:

The Riverdale #1, Augusta #2, and Augusta #3 tap stations will require increased station capacity to accommodate the additional capacity from SNG and Transco. The Riverdale #1 station capacity must be increased from 16,000 MCFH to 30,000 MCFH. The Augusta #2 station capacity must be increased from 647 MCFH to 1,300 MCFH. The Augusta #3 station capacity must be increased from 1,400 MCFH to 2,500 MCFH. The upgrade to the Riverdale LNG tap meter includes the replacement of the SNG metering facilities and the addition of the new Transco interconnect and metering. According to the petition for an amendment, this will allow for better utilization of the additional capacity from SNG and Transco. In addition, Brunswick/Bordertown tap station upgrades are needed to replace obsolete equipment, address MAOP reconfirmation issues, and increase capacity to support increasing customer usage in the area. 

Figure-2: Map of the Station Locations

AGL provided MFRs to supplement its requested amendment. The filed MFRs provided project details such as project locations, completion dates, and system reinforcement or pressure improvement issues being addressed. Figure 2 shows a map included in the MFRs.

The total project cost for upgrading all the stations is forecasted at $33.4 million.
Second Amendment for a 2025 – 2027 GRAM, Cherokee LNG, and SRR Capital Budget Combined Review Request

In the second amendment, AGL is requesting a combined review of the 2025 – 2027 GRAM, SRR, and Cherokee LNG Tracker capital budgets. The Company has recently forecasted that by the end of 2027, the GRAM capital budget will be underspent by $11.9 million. By the end of 2027, the Company has forecasted that SRR will be underspent by $62.8 million. The SRR underspending is a result of some projects being completed at costs lower than originally estimated. Project delays primarily due to challenges related to land access have also contributed to SRR underspending. 

If the first amendment is approved, the $33.4 million in station upgrades will reduce the SRR underspend of $62.8 million to $29.4 million. In addition, by the end of 2027, the Cherokee LNG Tracker capital budget is forecasted to overspend by $41.2 million. The remaining underspend of $29.4 million and the GRAM underspend of $11.9 million will cover the $41.2 million Cherokee LNG overspend. The Company stated in its petition that budget overspend is a result of the supply chain disruptions and inflationary labor and material increases associated with the pandemic.

By netting the capital budgets of GRAM, SRR, and Cherokee LNG Tracker, the overspending related to the Cherokee LNG Tracker capital budget will be absorbed by the underspending related to the GRAM and SRR capital budget. As a result, the aggregate capital budgets approved by the Stipulation are unaffected. Likewise, rate adjustments approved by the Stipulation are unaffected.

Staff Analysis

Staff provided substantial research and analysis as part of the collaboration with AGL, as discussed in Section-III above. As part of Staff’s due diligence on the official filing, Staff ensured that the filed documents matched the documents agreed to as part of the Staff and AGL collaboration. After review, Staff found no issues with the filed documents. 

Staff reviewed the MFRs and found them consistent with the MFR content provided in prior i-CDP filings. In reviewing the filed documents, Staff determined that a combined review of the three capital budgets was the best approach, as opposed to reallocating the underspend related to GRAM and SRR to the Cherokee LNG Tracker capital budget. Staff concluded that this approach would be more effective in ensuring that the overall approved budgets would not be exceeded. Staff determined that two amendments were required for the inclusion of new SRR projects and the combined capital budget review.
Commission Decision
